findings.title: The primary national quantity challenge is irrigation; the primary local growth challenge can be municipal or industrial
findings.evidence: Crop irrigation consumes about 75.7 Bgal/d in the 2010–20 model. Data-center direct water was about 0.048 Bgal/d in 2023 but is geographically concentrated and projected to grow quickly.
findings.implication: National policy charts and local siting charts need different denominators.

findings.title: Energy-water accounting can easily double count
findings.evidence: Power-sector cooling is already counted as thermoelectric water; attributing part of that water to data centers is useful but additive national totals are invalid.
findings.implication: The dashboard needs attribution views and physical-sector views with an explicit switch.

findings.title: Power-sector decarbonization changes water burdens as well as emissions
findings.evidence: Thermoelectric systems can have very high withdrawals but low consumption; desalination and AWG add electrical load, whose upstream water depends on the generation mix.
findings.implication: Future dashboard scenarios must link generation technology, cooling type, water source, hourly electricity, and seasonal basin stress.

findings.title: Climate risk changes both supply and demand
findings.evidence: Warming alters runoff/recharge and raises evaporative and irrigation demand; drought also reduces hydropower and river dilution while heat can raise electricity and cooling demand.
findings.implication: A supply-only forecast understates risk; charts need paired hydrology and demand scenarios.

findings.title: A physically present water source may be operationally unavailable
findings.evidence: Salinity, contamination, treatment failure, single-source conveyance, pumping restrictions, power loss, and insufficient storage can interrupt service without basin-wide depletion.
findings.implication: Risk maps need quantity, quality, infrastructure, legal, and governance layers rather than one scarcity score.

findings.title: Plastics policy savings must be product- and place-specific
findings.evidence: Industry boundaries are split, public deliveries are incomplete, and resin life-cycle water values vary across databases.
findings.implication: Prioritize bans or substitutions only after matching the same service and evaluating the replacement system in the affected watershed.

findings.title: Desalination and AWG solve different scales of problem
findings.evidence: Operating desalination plants deliver tens of millions of gallons per day; commercial AWGs deliver liters to thousands of liters per day and become energy-intensive at full household scale.
findings.implication: Desalination belongs in regional portfolio planning; AWG belongs mainly in drinking-water resilience and remote/emergency applications.
